scenes.heading: Batch Processing Use Cases
scenes.narration: Batch processing fits any workload where data can be gathered and processed in scheduled groups rather than the instant it arrives.

scenes.heading: Common batch use cases
bullets: Large ETL and data warehouse loads
scenes.narration: Nightly reporting is a classic batch use case, since dashboards only need to be fresh each morning. Billing and payroll runs fit batch because they naturally happen on a fixed cycle. Large ETL loads into a warehouse are batched to move huge volumes efficiently. And machine learning models are often retrained periodically on accumulated data rather than continuously.

scenes.heading: A nightly batch workflow
scenes.narration: Throughout the day, transactions and events accumulate in a source system. At night a scheduled job triggers and processes all of that data at once. By morning the reports and dashboards are refreshed and ready for the business.

scenes.text: Batch processing is ideal for scheduled, high-volume work like reporting, billing, and warehouse loads.
scenes.narration: The main lesson is that batch processing suits scheduled, high-volume tasks such as reporting, billing, and warehouse loads where instant results are not required.
